title: The Sunday Night Ritual That Makes Monday Mornings Effortless
audience: Office workers 25-40, professionals seeking Monday clarity

concept.hook: What separates people who dread Mondays from those who dominate them? It happens the night before.
concept.story_arc: Hook → The ritual concept → Brain dump (5min) → Outfit + bag (5min) → 3 priorities (10min) → Transformation → CTA

shots.prompt: Sunday evening. Person sits at a clean desk, journal open, pen in hand. Warm golden hour light through window. They look calm, purposeful. Close-up on their focused expression. A soft clock shows 7pm.
shots.camera: [Push in] Slow zoom from wide room shot to focused face
shots.narration: What separates people who dread Mondays from those who dominate them? It happens the night before.
shots.sfx: Soft evening ambient, pen writing sound

shots.prompt: Timelapse-style sequence: Person rapidly writing in journal, stress lines on face gradually smoothing out. Close-up of journal page filling with tasks, worries, commitments. Hand sweeps across page — releasing. Camera stays on face as tension visibly melts.
shots.camera: [Tracking shot] Smooth left-to-right tracking as journal fills
shots.narration: The first step is a brain dump. Take five minutes and write every unfinished task, every worry, every commitment onto paper. Don't organize. Don't prioritize. Just get it out of your head and onto the page. Your brain stops holding on when it knows the information is saved somewhere.

shots.prompt: Quick montage: clothes laid out on bed, bag packed by the door, laptop charger in bag. Everything is ready. Person walks through apartment — everything is in its place. Clean, calm, ready.
shots.camera: [Tilt down] Each item — clothes, bag, workspace — snapping into place
shots.narration: Step two: outfit and bag. Lay out Monday's clothes and pack your bag. This eliminates ten decisions before they even happen. Each morning decision drains willpower. The less you have to think about in the morning, the more thinking power you have for what actually matters.
shots.sfx: Zippers, drawer closing, soft thud of bag being set down

shots.prompt: Person writes three items on a notepad and places it beside the bed. Close-up on the notepad: '1. Client presentation, 2. Finish report, 3. Call mom.' They read it once, nod, and smile. Phone alarm set for 6:30am rings.
shots.camera: [Push in] Camera closes in on the three priorities as person reads them
shots.narration: Step three: three priorities. In ten minutes, identify the three most important outcomes for your week. Write them somewhere visible — beside your bed, on your bathroom mirror, as your phone wallpaper. When Monday starts with clarity, you don't start reactive. You start dominant.

shots.prompt: Monday morning. Sunrise through window. Same person, calm expression, coffee in hand. Wide establishing shot — they walk out the door with confidence, bag packed, outfit ready, shoulders back. Golden morning light.
shots.camera: [Pull out] Wide establishing shot, morning sun flares gently
shots.narration: Twenty minutes Sunday saves two hours of Monday morning scrambling. Your future Monday self will walk out that door with clarity and confidence — because you did the work the night before. Subscribe for more science-backed productivity routines.
shots.sfx: Morning birds, door closing gently, ambient swell

metadata.youtube_description:
What separates people who dread Mondays from those who dominate them? It happens the night before. In 20 minutes on Sunday night, you can eliminate Monday morning decision fatigue and start the week with clarity and confidence.

📌 What you'll learn:
- The 5-minute brain dump that frees cognitive RAM
- Why laying out clothes saves 10 decisions worth of willpower
- The 3-priority method for week-starting clarity
- A complete 20-minute Sunday ritual you can start tonight

00:38 — 3 priorities (10 min)
00:58 — Monday transformation
